title: Over a field, few differentials at a point imply smoothness there
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\Omega_{S/k}$ be the module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. If $$\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)\le\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S),$$ then $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]: there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $S_g$ is a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), implication (2) => (1), proof lines 38641-38681; tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00TT,algebra-lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field)

proof.text: (The algebraically closed field.) Write $\kappa=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a field extension of $k$ through $k\to S\to\kappa$. Let $K$ be an algebraic closure of $\kappa$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] with its field homomorphism $\psi:\kappa\to K$; then $K$ is an algebraically closed field extension of $k$ through $k\to S\to\kappa\xrightarrow{\psi}K$ [def-pc-field-extension] carrying a $k$-algebra map $\psi$ from $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, as the source asks. Put $S_K=K\otimes_kS$, a $K$-algebra through $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes1$, with $j:S\to S_K$, $s\mapsto1\otimes s$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. If $s_1,\dots,s_n$ generate $S$ as a $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], then $1\otimes s_1,\dots,1\otimes s_n$ generate $S_K$ as a $K$-algebra, since $\lambda\otimes p(s_1,\dots,s_n)=\lambda\,p(1\otimes s_1,\dots,1\otimes s_n)$ for a polynomial $p$ over $k$ and the $\lambda\otimes s$ span $S_K$; so $S_K$ is a finite type $K$-algebra.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), lines 38652-38655

proof.text: (The point $\mathfrak m$ over $\mathfrak q$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (2), applied to the $k$-algebra maps $\mathrm{id}_K:K\to K$ and $S\to\kappa\xrightarrow{\psi}K$, there is a $k$-algebra map $\phi:S_K\to K$ with $\phi(\lambda\otimes s)=\lambda\,\psi(\bar s)$, $\bar s$ the image of $s$ in $\kappa$; this is the composite $S_K\to K\otimes_k\kappa\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_K\otimes\psi}K$ of the source. It is $K$-linear and surjective ($\phi(\lambda\otimes1)=\lambda$), so $\mathfrak m=\ker\phi$ is a maximal ideal of $S_K$ with $S_K/\mathfrak m\cong K$; hence the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=(S_K)_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak m(S_K)_{\mathfrak m}\cong S_K/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is $K$, with $S_K\to\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ equal to $\phi$. Moreover $\phi(j(s))=\psi(\bar s)$, and $\psi$ is injective (a homomorphism of fields), so $j^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\{s:\bar s=0\}=\mathfrak q$: $\mathfrak m$ lies over $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), lines 38655-38664

proof.text: (Dimensions.) By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension] for $k\to K$, the finite type $k$-algebra $S$ and the prime $\mathfrak m$ of $S_K$ lying over $\mathfrak q$ (step 2), $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\dim_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}S_K)$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]; that node writes $S\otimes_kK$, and the swap $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes s$ is an isomorphism of $K$-algebras compatible with the maps from $S$, so it carries the prime over $\mathfrak q$ to $\mathfrak m$ and induces a homeomorphism of spectra, which preserves dimensions at corresponding points. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring] for the field $K$, the finite type $K$-algebra $S_K$ (step 1) and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, $\dim_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}S_K)=\dim((S_K)_{\mathfrak m})$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Hence $$\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\dim((S_K)_{\mathfrak m}).$$

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), lines 38664-38669 (citing Lemma 00P4 lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension and Lemma 00OU lemma-dimension-closed-point-finite-type-field)

proof.text: (Differentials.) By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] for $k\to K$ and $k\to S$, $\Omega_{S_K/K}\cong S_K\otimes_S\Omega_{S/k}$ as $S_K$-modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Tensoring with $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=K$ over $S_K$ (step 2) and using associativity, $\Omega_{S_K/K}\otimes_{S_K}\kappa(\mathfrak m)\cong\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_SK$, where $S$ acts on $K$ through $\phi\circ j=\psi\circ(S\to\kappa)$; since this map factors through $\kappa=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_SK\cong(\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa)\otimes_\kappa K$, the extension of scalars of the $\kappa$-vector space $V=\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa$ along $\psi$. A basis $(e_i)$ of $V$ gives the basis $(e_i\otimes1)$ of $V\otimes_\kappa K$, so $$\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak m)}\Omega_{S_K/K}\otimes_{S_K}\kappa(\mathfrak m)=\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q).$$ (The source first replaces $S$ by a principal localization $S_g$ on which $\Omega_{S/k}$ is generated by at most $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ elements, by Nakayama, and transports this generator bound; only the fibre dimension at $\mathfrak m$ enters the next step, and the equality above gives it directly, so that detour is not needed.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), lines 38646-38651 and 38670-38673 (citing Lemma 00DV lemma-NAK and Lemma 00RV lemma-differentials-base-change)

proof.text: (Smooth after base change.) By steps 4, the hypothesis and step 3, $$\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak m)}\Omega_{S_K/K}\otimes_{S_K}\kappa(\mathfrak m)=\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)\le\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\dim((S_K)_{\mathfrak m}).$$ $K$ is algebraically closed, $S_K$ is a finite type $K$-algebra (step 1) and $\mathfrak m$ is a maximal ideal of $S_K$ (step 2), so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-maximal-ideal-alg-closed-differentials-bound] gives that $K\to S_K$ is smooth at $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), lines 38673-38675 (citing Lemma 00TS lemma-characterize-smooth-kbar, (2) => (4))

proof.text: (Descent.) By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-field-extension-descent] for the field extension $K/k$ of step 1, the finite type $k$-algebra $S$, the prime $\mathfrak q_K=\mathfrak m$ of $S_K=K\otimes_kS$ and $j^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q$ (step 2), smoothness of $K\to S_K$ at $\mathfrak m$ (step 5) implies that $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]: there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $S_g$ a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].
